s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory illness with fever and shortness of breath
salient_findings: Fever up to 39°C
Anosmia
Shortness of breath
Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
Coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Bilateral multifocal pneumonia on chest radiography
key_facts: Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
Coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction
Chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia
Normal sinus rhythm with normal frontal QRS axis on ECG

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory illness with fever and shortness of breath
salient_findings: Fever up to 39°C
Anosmia
Shortness of breath
Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
Coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Bilateral multifocal pneumonia on chest radiography
key_facts: Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
Coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction
Chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia
Normal sinus rhythm with normal frontal QRS axis on ECG

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, anosmia, and shortness of breath, combined with the nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction and chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia, are consistent with COVID-19.

rejected.label: Aspiration pneumonia
rejected.why: While the patient has risk factors for aspiration pneumonia, such as morbid obesity and obstructive sleep apnea, the presence of anosmia and the positive nasopharyngeal swab suggest a viral etiology.

rejected.label: Influenza pneumonia
rejected.why: Although influenza pneumonia could present with similar symptoms, the specific combination of anosmia, fever, and radiographic findings, along with the positive nasopharyngeal swab, points more strongly towards COVID-19.

rejected.label: Pneumococcal pneumonia
rejected.why: Pneumococcal pneumonia typically presents with lobar consolidation on imaging and does not typically cause anosmia, making it less likely in this case.

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient's low oxygen saturation and bilateral multifocal pneumonia could suggest acute respiratory distress syndrome, this is more of a clinical syndrome than a specific diagnosis, and the underlying cause appears to be COVID-19.
